battle.name: 宰德·本·阿里的起義
battle.brief: 公元七四〇年，宰德·本·阿里在伊拉克庫法舉兵反對倭馬亞朝，追索侯賽因殉難之血；同年底其子易卜拉欣在巴士拉響應，被總督優素福·伊本·歐麥爾圍困四十日而平。斯巴達長矛的雙手直刺形制，在此役以阿拉伯步兵與騎兵長矛之姿延續：街巷短兵與城外單挑，都靠矛尖定生死。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 這是一場倭馬亞哈里發國在伊拉克前線的平叛戰役，交戰兩方的力量對比懸殊。倭馬亞一方由大馬士革的哈里發希沙姆·伊本·阿卜杜勒·馬利克直接遙控：七四〇年他坐鎮敘利亞，把伊拉克當作帝國的邊陲，指派總督優素福·伊本·歐麥爾·阿爾·菲赫里節制庫法、巴士拉兩城；總督之下有各城守備、稅吏與軍需官，軍隊以部落徵召的騎兵為骨幹，兵源來自敘利亞、阿拉伯沙漠與伊拉克本身的部落。用兵上，倭馬亞方靠的是文書、津貼與城防：敘利亞來的增援一旦上路，庫法到巴士拉約一百五十公里的幼發拉底河下游驛道就成了補給線。起義一方沒有軍隊，只有一張網。核心是哈希姆家系的阿里後裔，以宰德·本·阿里為旗幟；外圍是庫法的什葉派支持者、胡阿里吉派志士，以及受壓抑的波斯歸信者（馬瓦利），他們在巴士拉人數眾多，卻不屬於任何阿拉伯部落。最後是也門系阿拉伯部落，如哈南與蘇萊姆兩族，庫法城內此二族曾參與卡巴拉之戰，此番再度站在阿里家族一邊。聯盟內部並無統一編制：庫法由宰德自領，巴士拉由其子易卜拉欣另立旗號，實際戰鬥多由胡阿里吉派與馬瓦利武裝擔當，彼此靠密使與同一套宗教口號維繫，沒有後勤，也沒有攻城器械，這正是此役最要命的地方。
countriesEn: This was a suppression campaign fought on the forward line of the Umayyad caliphate in Iraq, and the two sides were grotesquely mismatched. On the Umayyad side the caliph Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik in Damascus gave direct orders: in 740 he sat in Syria, treated Iraq as the frontier of his rule, and left the governorship of Kufa and Basra to Yusuf ibn Umar al-Thaqafi, with the city garrisons, tax clerks and munitions officers under him. His army was in the first instance tribal levies of cavalry, raised in Syria, in the Arabian desert and from the Iraqi tribes themselves. In practice the Umayyads fought with paperwork, subsidies and fortifications; once reinforcements came down from Syria, the road along the lower Euphrates, roughly one hundred and fifty kilometres from Kufa to Basra, became the supply line. The side that rose had no army, only a web. Its core was the Alids, the descendants of Hashim, with Zayd ibn Ali as the figurehead; around him stood the Shi'i partisans of Kufa, the Kharijite volunteers, and the mawali, the Persian converts, who were oppressed and counted for little, and who were numerous in Basra without belonging to any Arab tribe. Finally there were the Yamani Arab clans such as Hanan and Sulaym, the two great Kufan clans that had fought at Karbala and now stood once more on the side of Ali's house. The coalition had no unified establishment. In Kufa Zayd commanded in person; in Basra his son Ibrahim raised a separate banner; the actual fighting was in the hands of Kharijite and mawali bands. What held the alliance together were messengers and a shared religious slogan; there was no logistics and no siege train, and that was the decisive weakness of the whole rising.
people: 宰德·本·阿里·伊本·侯賽因·伊本·阿里·伊本·阿比·塔利卜，哈希姆家第五代，早年以「先知之友」聞名，是第四任伊馬目阿里·本·侯賽因之子、第五任伊馬目穆罕默德·巴基爾之兄。他出生在侯賽因殉難後的年月，阿里家的骨肉在倭馬亞的監視之下生活；他曾居於麥地那，也因拒絕承認倭馬亞哈里發而長期受看管。相傳哈里發歐麥爾二世在位時曾允諾由阿里家繼承哈里發位，並把女兒嫁與宰德之兄葉齊德；歐麥爾二世一死，葉齊德隨即暴卒，許諾被倭馬亞政權收回，宰德失去一次以和平方式取得權位的機會，家族對倭馬亞的怨恨自此加深。他身邊還有胡阿里吉派與什葉派的支持者，庫法與巴士拉的胡阿里吉派主事者、以及在清真寺裏號召起義的講道者，在記載中多以匿名或綽號出現。宰德陣中最重要的人物是易卜拉欣·本·宰德，其子，主持巴士拉方面的起義，被推為當地信眾的伊馬目；以及歐拜德·阿拉·本·宰德·阿爾卡比，庫法望族，率巴士拉義軍在城外擊潰總督騎兵。倭馬亞方則是優素福·伊本·歐麥爾·阿爾·菲赫里，此人原是歐麥爾的釋奴，靠鎮壓伊拉克的阿里派起家，經歷過多次起義，是哈里發手中對付伊拉克最有效的將領之一；他後來在與哈里發的失和中倒向阿拔斯運動，最終被處死。
peopleEn: Zayd ibn Ali ibn Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib was the fifth generation of the house of Hashim, famous from early on as the Friend of the Prophet; he was the son of the fourth Imam, Ali ibn al-Husayn, and the brother of the fifth Imam, Muhammad al-Baqir. He was born in the years after Husayn's death at Karbala, and the family of Ali lived under Umayyad surveillance; he spent time in Medina, and for refusing to acknowledge the Umayyad caliphate he was kept under watch for long stretches. It is said that under Caliph Umar II, from 717 to 720, the Alids were promised the caliphate, and that Umar's own daughter was married to Zayd's brother Yahya; when Umar II died and Yahya died shortly afterwards, the promise was withdrawn and the Umayyads closed the road by which Zayd might have taken the office in peace. That memory is the immediate occasion of the rising of 740. Around him were the Kharijite leaders and the Shi'i partisans of Kufa; the heads of the Basra Kharijites and the preachers who called for the rising in the great mosque of Kufa appear in the sources mostly as unnamed figures or by nicknames. The most important figures on the rebel side were Ibrahim ibn Zayd, his son, who led the rising in Basra and was acknowledged as imam there, and Ubayd Allah ibn Zayd al-Ka'bi, a Kufan notable who led the Basra rebel army and broke the governor's cavalry in the field outside the walls. On the Umayyad side stood Yusuf ibn Umar al-Thaqafi, a former mawla of Umar who had risen through the suppression of the Iraqi Alids and had handled more than one rising; he was one of the most effective instruments in the caliph's hands in Iraq. He later threw in his lot with the Abbasid movement in his quarrel with the caliph, and was put to death.
kits: 這場戰役裡沒有希臘人，但戰場上最不缺的就是矛。斯巴達長矛本身是公元前八世紀以降重裝步兵的裝備：白蠍松木的長柄、葉形鐵矛頭、尾端一枚銅套，兩手握持，靠軀幹的重量把矛尖送出去。公元七四〇年早已沒有任何軍隊配發這樣的東西，但同一套設計邏輯——直柄、雙手、一擊定生死的刺擊——在伊拉克的兵卒手裡以另一個名字活著：阿拉伯語叫「密薩爾」，即長矛，是步兵列隊的骨幹，也是騎兵中「攜矛者」的主要兵器。巴士拉與庫法的義軍多為臨時徵集的民眾與退伍士兵，手上多數只有短矛、標槍與柴刀；正因長矛短缺，叛軍在街巷與城門的爭奪才格外依賴近身刺擊。其餘裝備的形制與七、八世紀之交的伊拉克完全一致：弓是複合反曲的胡拉沙尼式，箭為短桿骨鏃，義軍靠它覆蓋屋頂與街口；刀劍既有直刃彎刀，也有阿拉伯式的弧形軍刀；盾牌以圓形木胎蒙皮與騎兵的高身皮盾為主；鎧甲是鎖子甲與鱗甲，頭盔多為鐵製，帶護鼻與護頰。攻城一方最吃虧的地方正在這裏：優素福的兵既無大型配重投石機，也無成熟的圍城技藝，只能靠封鎖與飢餓，這也是巴士拉僵持四十日的原因之一。義軍則在城外挖壕溝，以土堤隔斷陸路，又在沼澤邊緣的支汊上設障，把攻城軍擋在濕地裏。從最簡單的工具到最講究的鎧甲，此役兩邊的差距都集中在同一點：能不能把裝備配齊。
kitsEn: There are no Greeks in this war, but spears are the last thing the battlefield lacks. The Spartan dory itself is the equipment of heavy infantry from the eighth century BCE onward: a white-pine shaft, a leaf-shaped iron head, a bronze butt-cap at the foot, gripped with both hands and driven forward by the weight of the body. By 740 CE no army in the world was still issuing such a weapon, but the same design logic, straight shaft, two hands, one thrust that decides life or death, lived on in the hands of the Iraqi soldiers under another name. In Arabic it is the mith'al, the long spear, the backbone of the infantry line and the principal weapon of the cavalry who rode with a spear couched. Most of the men raised in Basra and Kufa were hastily levied townsmen and discharged soldiers who possessed little more than short spears, javelins and farm knives; it was precisely the shortage of long spears that made the rebels' street and gate fighting depend so heavily on thrusting at close quarters. The rest of the equipment fits the early medieval Iraqi pattern exactly. The bows were composite recurved bows of the Khurasani type, with short shafts and bone or horn heads, and the rebels relied on them to sweep the rooftops and the mouths of the streets. The blades were a mixture of straight-edged swords and the curved Arab saif. The shields were round wooden ones faced with hide for the infantry, and the tall hide-covered turs of the cavalry. Armour was mail and scale, with iron helmets fitted with nasal and cheek guards. The besieging side was worst off in precisely this respect: Yusuf's men had neither great counterweight trebuchets nor a mature siege craft, and could rely on nothing but blockade and starvation, which is one reason the stalemate at Basra lasted forty days. The rebels, for their part, dug a trench outside the walls, cut the land approaches with earth banks, and obstructed the side channels at the edge of the marsh, keeping the besiegers out in the wetlands. From the simplest tools to the most elaborate armour, the difference between the two sides in this war came down to one question: could the equipment be supplied and matched.
tactics: 庫法的起事是一場典型的清真寺政治與街巷戰。宰德依賴庫法大清真寺作為集結點與號召場所；總督得知陰謀後，命令民眾集於大清真寺、閉門搜查，試圖在人群裡找出宰德，逼得支持者四散。宰德帶少數人反攻清真寺，號召民眾出來應援，有人說這與數十年前侯賽因在卡巴拉的處境如出一轍。支持者大批倒戈，宰德退入清真寺一隅再戰，最終在近身混戰中被流矢射中額頭。巴士拉方面是另一種打法。易卜拉欣與歐拜德·阿拉利用巴士拉城本身的防禦：關閉城門、封鎖通往波斯灣的沼澤道路、在陸路方向挖壕設障，把優素福的圍軍困在濕地與鹽鹼地之間，攻城軍既缺水又缺糧，被迫後退。義軍隨即主動出擊，在沒有城池遮蔽的開闊地與總督的騎兵交鋒——這是全役唯一一次大規模野戰——據敘述義軍一度擊潰敵騎，總督本人亦受傷。倭馬亞方沒有足夠兵力四面合圍，只能退守封鎖線，把攻城變成圍困，時間一度站在義軍一邊；但義軍同樣缺乏攻擊能力，最終因糧援斷絕而崩潰。換句話說，庫法靠的是清真寺裏的群眾與一場近身刺擊，巴士拉靠的是一道壕溝與一次漂亮的野戰反擊。兩處的共同點是：長矛在窄處頂住對方，在開闊處卻被騎兵繞開。
tacticsEn: The rising in Kufa was politics fought in a mosque and in the streets. Zayd relied on the great mosque of Kufa as his place of assembly and his platform. When the governor learned of the plot, he ordered the people to gather in the great mosque, shut the doors and began a search, trying to pick Zayd out of the crowd; the supporters scattered. Zayd fought his way back to the mosque with a small band and called on the people to come out, and the parallel with Husayn's abandonment at Karbala decades before was noticed at the time. Supporters deserted in mass, and Zayd was reduced to fighting in a corner of the mosque until he was struck in the forehead by an arrow during the close fighting. Basra was fought in a different fashion. Ibrahim ibn Zayd and Ubayd Allah used the defences of the city itself: the gates were shut, the road through the marshes toward the Persian Gulf was cut, a trench and earthworks were dug across the land approaches, and the besieging army was pinned among wetlands and salt flats, short of water and short of food, and forced to fall back. The rebels then took the offensive into the open plain outside the walls and fought the governor's cavalry there, the only set-piece field battle of the war, and the accounts say the rebel horse broke the enemy and the governor himself was wounded. The Umayyads did not have the men to invest the city on all sides, so they fell back onto the blockade line and turned the assault into a siege, and time began to favour the rebels. But the rebels had no offensive power of their own, and their coalition finally collapsed as the food ran out. In short: Kufa was decided by a crowd in a mosque and by a single close thrust; Basra was decided by a trench and by one clean counter-stroke in the open field. The two shared one common feature: the long spear held the line in the narrow places and was run round by cavalry in the open.
data: 關於數字必須先說明一點：這場戰役的主要記述來自八、九世紀的伊拉克地方史家與什葉派傳記，數目多有誇大，讀時宜取其量級。可靠的骨架是這樣的：起義的爆發點在公元七四〇年一月六日，即回曆一二二年薩法爾月十日；宰德在同月初二陣亡於庫法；巴士拉的圍城戰則自同年年底延續到翌年，歷時約四十日。地理上，庫法與巴士拉之間沿幼發拉底下游的道路約一百五十公里，消息與援兵都得走上兩三日；由伊拉克把首級送往大馬士革，走的是約一千三百公里的商隊路。兵員方面，傳記稱宰德在巴士拉一帶把一萬五千人登記入軍籍，庫法方面的說法則是「一萬名戰士」隨時可用；實際聚兵遠少於此，他在庫法的支持者在他孤軍苦戰時大批倒戈，最後隨身只剩下數十人。倭馬亞方面在伊拉克的守軍不過數百，優素福自巴士拉出動的討伐部隊也只是總督與隨從數百之眾，雙方在紙面人數上都是小打小鬥，卻在巴士拉城外打成全役最激烈的一戰。傷亡沒有可信的統計：敘述多只逐一點名陣亡的將領，如納斯爾·伊本·哈齊瑪·阿巴西、歐拜德·伊本·祖拉拉等；至於義軍被處決者的總數，各家說法從數百到數千不等，彼此矛盾，不宜引用為定數。戰後的處理卻有具體時序可循：宰德的遺體被秘密安葬在庫法城外，事後被掘出，釘在十字架上示眾三年；直到哈里發希沙姆去世，其後繼者下令焚屍，灰燼投入幼發拉底河；阿拔斯人在七五〇年奪位後掘出希沙姆的遺體，以釘十字架與焚燒回敬。
dataEn: About the numbers, one caveat has to come first: the principal accounts of this war come from ninth- and tenth-century Iraqi local historians and from Shi'i biographical tradition, and their figures are often inflated, so they are best read as orders of magnitude. The reliable skeleton is this: the revolt broke out on 6 January 740 CE, that is 10 Safar 122 AH, and Zayd was killed in Kufa on 2 Safar 122 AH; the siege of Basra ran through the end of that year and into the next and lasted about forty days. Geographically, the road along the lower Euphrates between Kufa and Basra is about one hundred and fifty kilometres, so news and reinforcements took two or three days to travel; carrying the head from Iraq to Damascus meant a caravan route of some thirteen hundred kilometres. On numbers of men, the accounts claim that fifteen thousand were enrolled on Zayd's army register in the Basra region, while the Kufa version speaks of ten thousand warriors ready at a moment's notice. The real numbers were far smaller: at Kufa his supporters deserted him in droves as he fought alone, and he ended the day with only a few dozen men. The Umayyad garrison in Iraq numbered only a few hundred, and the force Yusuf ibn Umar took out of Basra to hunt the rebels was the governor himself and a few hundred followers. Both sides were therefore small operations in paper terms, yet they collided in the most violent engagement of the war outside Basra. There is no credible casualty count: the narratives usually name individual officers among the dead, such as Nasr ibn Khazima al-Abasi and Amr ibn Zurara, while the total number of rebels executed is given anywhere from hundreds to thousands, the versions contradicting one another, and none of them should be quoted as a settled figure. What can be traced with some precision is the sequence of the aftermath: Zayd's body was buried in secret outside Kufa, then dug up and crucified for public display for three years; after the death of the caliph Hisham his successor ordered the corpse burned and the ashes thrown into the Euphrates; when the Abbasids took power in 750, they exhumed Hisham's body and repaid the debt by crucifying and burning it in the same way.
cause: 三股力量在七四〇年的伊拉克匯合，才有了這場起義。第一是阿里家的正統主張。侯賽因在卡巴拉被殺之後，哈希姆一家有權繼承哈里發，在伊拉克什葉派中已成為公開的政治要求；宰德作為第四任伊馬目之子、第五任伊馬目之兄，是最有資格挑起這面旗的人。歐麥爾二世在位時曾允諾由阿里家繼承哈里發位，並將女兒嫁給宰德之兄葉齊德；歐麥爾二世一死、葉齊德暴卒，許諾被倭馬亞政權收回，家族的路被堵死，這一段記憶直接構成本場起義的近因。第二是胡阿里吉派的革命宣教。胡阿里吉派在伊拉克南部與巴士拉一帶傳播「必須起身討伐不義的哈里發」的主張，認為對倭馬亞的聖戰是每個信士的義務，庫法與巴士拉的清真寺裡這套說辭已有多年根基。宰德起初對立刻舉旗猶豫，他不願接受胡阿里吉派要求立即公布對馬瓦利全面豁免與平等待遇的綱領，這一拖延在後世記述中被視為致命。第三是波斯歸信者的處境。伊拉克南部的馬瓦利人數眾多、納稅負擔重，在阿拉伯人的政治與軍隊中居於附屬地位；第七、八世紀之交帝國由向外擴張轉入內部治理，邊軍不再大量吸納他們，經濟與政治上的退潮讓這批人轉向支持以什葉派旗號進行的反倭馬亞運動。第四個背景是敘利亞政局：哈里發希沙姆的統治在七三〇年代並不穩固，還要應付北非與安達盧斯的戰事，因此伊拉克的平叛準備從來不充分——這是起義得以迅速蔓延的結構性原因。
causeEn: Three currents met in Iraq in 740, and it was their conjunction that produced the rising. The first was the Alid claim to legitimate rule. Since Husayn's death at Karbala, the proposition that the house of Hashim had a right to the caliphate had become an open political demand among the Shi'i of Iraq, and Zayd, as son of the fourth Imam and brother of the fifth, was the man with the strongest title to raise that flag. Under Umar II the Alids had been promised the caliphate and Umar's daughter had been married to Zayd's brother Yahya; when Umar II died and Yahya died soon after, the promise was withdrawn by the Umayyad state and the family's road was blocked. That memory is the immediate cause of the rising of 740. The second was Kharijite revolutionary preaching. In southern Iraq and Basra the Kharijites had spread the doctrine that it was the duty of the faithful to rise in arms against an unjust caliph, that jihad against the Umayyads was owed by every believer, and the great mosques of Kufa and Basra had absorbed that argument for years. Zayd at first hesitated to raise the banner; he was unwilling to adopt at once the Kharijite programme, which demanded the immediate promulgation of a general amnesty for the mawali and of full equality for the Persian converts, and in later accounts this delay is treated as the fatal flaw. The third was the position of the Persian converts. The mawali were numerous in southern Iraq and heavily taxed, and stood in a subordinate position in the politics and the armies of the Arabs. As the caliphate turned from outward expansion to internal administration around the turn of the eighth century, and the frontier armies stopped absorbing them in large numbers, the economic and political ebb pushed these people towards a Shi'i-bannered opposition to the Umayyads. A fourth background factor is Syria: Hisham's government was itself unstable in the 730s, still committed to wars in North Africa and al-Andalus, and preparations for quelling trouble in Iraq were never adequate. That structural weakness is the reason the rising spread as fast as it did.
impact: 起義本身的時間很短，卻在政治上留下幾道長疤。第一，什葉派從此有了一個可以效法的模式：以「先知的後裔」的名義、以清真寺的集結為起點、以武力爭奪哈里發權為目標。四十年後阿拔斯朝境內的阿里派起義，即穆罕默德·納夫斯·扎基耶在麥加的舉兵，幾乎照抄了這套劇本，說明七四〇年的教訓是有效的。第二，宰德的形象被系統地塑造為殉道者。什葉派十二伊馬目派把他視為起義的首領與「盟約之劍」的持有者，據說侯賽因出發前曾把這柄劍托付給他；他的名字成為後來也門宰德派的教派名號來源。宰德派主張有資格的阿里後裔都可以像宰德那樣以起義與言論取得伊馬目位，與十二伊馬目派「指派」的主張分歧開來，源頭正是七四〇年。第三，聯盟的破裂留下了整整三條路線。宰德起義把胡阿里吉派、阿里派與阿拔斯派拉到同一面旗幟下，也讓它們在共同的失敗中看清彼此的算盤：胡阿里吉派主張極端的橫向革命，什葉派要求的是溫和的清真寺式轉移，阿拔斯派要的則是哈里發權本身；這一分裂在八世紀中葉演成伊斯梅伊利、宰德與阿拔斯三條互相否定的道路。第四，倭馬亞的政策從此更嚴：希沙姆致函希加茲與敘利亞的部落，警告不得支持叛軍，違者以兵戈相向；伊拉克境內阿里派分子的家屬被連坐、被迫遷徙，阿里派的鬥爭從公開的舉兵轉為地下結社與零星刺殺。最後一筆帳在阿拔斯朝：七五〇年之後，執政者把七四〇年的清算視為合法的報復，掘出希沙姆遺體釘十字架焚燒，阿里派的殉難記憶從此成為推翻倭馬亞的宣傳動員。換個角度看，這場失敗正是阿拔斯革命的前奏：先由胡阿里吉派與阿里派在伊拉克反覆消耗倭馬亞的兵力和合法性，再由阿拔斯派收割。
impactEn: The rising was short, but it left several deep political scars. First, the Shi'a acquired a repeatable model: take the name of the Prophet's descendant, gather in the mosque, and contest the caliphate by force. The Alid rising inside Abbasid territory forty years later, the revolt of Muhammad al-Nafs al-Zakiyya in Mecca, copied this scenario almost line for line, which shows that the lesson of 740 had been learned. Second, Zayd's image was systematically shaped as that of a martyr. The Twelver Shi'a hold him as the leader of the rising and the keeper of the Sword of the Pledge, said to have been entrusted to him by Husayn before he set out; his name became the source of the name of the Zaydiyya sect in Yemen, whose doctrine is that any qualified descendant of Ali can obtain the imamate by asserting the claim and fighting for it, the very thing Zayd did, and that is precisely where it parts company with the Twelver doctrine of divine appointment. Third, the rupture of the coalition left three roads behind. The rising of Zayd had pulled the Kharijites, the Alids and the Abbasids under one banner, and it also let them see one another's arithmetic in the course of a shared failure: the Kharijites wanted an extreme and horizontal revolution, the Shi'i wanted a moderate transfer of authority through the mosques, and the Abbasids wanted the caliphate itself. That split matured in the mid-eighth century into the three mutually exclusive paths of Ismailism, Zaydism and the Abbasid claim. Fourth, Umayyad policy tightened. Hisham sent letters to the tribes of the Hijaz and Syria warning them not to support the rebels and threatening the sword against them; in Iraq the families of the Alids were placed under collective watch and compelled to move away, and the Alid movement turned from open insurrection into clandestine association and scattered acts of violence. The last account belongs to the Abbasids: after 750 the new rulers treated the settlement of 740 as a legitimate debt, exhuming Hisham's body and crucifying and burning it. The memory of Alid martyrdom thus became propaganda for the overthrow of the Umayyads. Seen from the other side, this failure was the prelude to the Abbasid revolution: the Kharijites and the Alids first wore down the Umayyad army and legitimacy in Iraq through repeated revolts, and the Abbasids harvested the result.
result: 結果是徹底的失敗，而且失敗得很快。庫法方面：宰德在公眾面前號召之後，支持者如卡巴拉時那樣成批倒向倭馬亞方，最後跟隨他衝向清真寺的只剩數十人；他在近身戰中被一枝射中額頭的流矢重創，取箭時傷勢失控而死，年四十二歲。屍體一度秘密葬在庫法城外，隨後被倭馬亞當局掘出，釘上十字架示眾三年，屍身腐爛後才被移走；其後繼者再將其焚化，灰燼投入幼發拉底河。巴士拉方面：易卜拉欣據城抵抗，圍城約四十日，糧援斷絕，義軍內部崩潰，出城談判後被捕，與大批追隨者遭處決；巴士拉城被劫掠，總督優素福後來既受封賞又被哈里發責其用兵遲緩，數月內即被撤換。庫法以東的呼羅珊：宰德之子葉齊德在七四二至七四三年於此再舉旗響應，據載所部不過七十人，隨即被納斯爾·伊本·賽亞爾與哈卡姆·伊本·薩勒特鎮壓，葉齊德被殺，屍體被送回庫法示眾。從軍事的角度看，這場戰役沒有任何一方取得戰略成果：倭馬亞方以數百人平了兩座城的叛亂，代價是把整個伊拉克的防務信用押在一位總督的個人能力上；起義方則丟掉了最寶貴的家族象徵、最忠誠的幹部和唯一一次把什葉派旗號舉到伊拉克城頭的機會。八世紀上半葉，則是倭馬亞治下伊拉克最後一次大規模阿里派叛亂，此後阿里派的鬥爭轉入地下，為阿拔斯人的接管讓出了空間。
resultEn: The result was complete failure, and it came quickly. In Kufa: after Zayd called the people out, his supporters deserted to the Umayyads in mass, as they had at Karbala, and only a few dozen men followed him as he charged at the mosque; in the close fighting he was fatally wounded by an arrow that struck his forehead, and died as the arrow was being drawn. The body was buried in secret outside Kufa, then dug up by the Umayyad authorities and crucified for display for three years, until it had rotted and was removed; his successor then ordered it burned and the ashes thrown into the Euphrates. In Basra: Ibrahim held the city through a siege of about forty days; when supplies ran out the rebel ranks disintegrated, the men came out to parley and were taken, and Ibrahim was executed with a large number of his followers; Basra was sacked, and Yusuf ibn Umar, though rewarded, was blamed by the caliph for the slowness of his operations and was removed within months. To the east, in Khurasan: Zayd's son Yahya raised the banner again in 742 and 743; the accounts give him no more than seventy men, and he was immediately pinned down and destroyed by Nasr ibn Sayyar and Hakim ibn Salt, and killed, his body being carried back to Kufa and displayed. From a purely military point of view neither side gained anything from this war. The Umayyads suppressed two revolts with a few hundred men, at the price of staking the credibility of the whole Iraqi defence on one governor's personal ability; the rebels lost their most precious family symbol, their most loyal cadres, and the only chance to raise the Shi'i banner over an Iraqi city. For the first half of the eighth century this was the last large Alid revolt in Umayyad Iraq; after it, Alid struggle went underground and left the field open for the Abbasids.
